extracted.intended_audience: apprenticeship program sponsors, Registration Agencies, State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs), participating employers, and administrators responsible for registering and operating registered apprenticeship programs
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and required elements for establishing, registering, operating, and evaluating registered apprenticeship programs and apprenticeship agreements under the Office of Apprenticeship (OA) and recognized State Apprenticeship Agencies (SAAs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Apprenticeship responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will establish and maintain an Office of Apprenticeship (OA) to facilitate administration and coordination of the National Apprenticeship System and to perform specified functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA functions include: (a) formulating/updating regulations, guidance, policies, procedures; (b) registering and overseeing apprenticeship programs and standards that satisfy this part and part 30; (c) promoting development of industry-validated standards and National Occupational Standards; (d) recognizing and overseeing SAAs that satisfy requirements; (e) maintaining and making publicly available National Apprenticeship System data; (f) promoting diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, and enforcing equal opportunity standards; (g) providing technical assistance to sponsors, SAAs, and stakeholders; (h) engaging stakeholders and developing partnerships to expand quality apprenticeship programs; (i) conducting other activities that support the National Apprenticeship System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: No provision in this part supersedes any Federal, State, or local law establishing minimum labor standards of apprenticeship that are higher or more protective of apprentices than those in this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, nothing in this part or apprenticeship agreements invalidates apprenticeship provisions in collective bargaining agreements that are more protective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: If a court holds any portion of this part invalid, the remaining provisions will be construed to give maximum lawful effect; severable provisions won't affect the remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition compliance deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitional rules for occupations and program registrations after the effective date of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key transitional items: §29.7 applies after 90 days for occupations not previously determined; programs not previously registered by OA must seek registration when electronic submission is available; programs registered prior to electronic process must meet new requirements before converting to permanent registration; programs registered by OA prior to effective date must comply with Subpart A within 2 years; existing SAAs recognized as of effective date continue to be recognized until Dec 31, 2026, with related conditions for State Apprenticeship Plans and SAA-specific occupations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Related instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Organized and systematic instruction designed to provide apprentices knowledge of theoretical and technical subjects related to the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be delivered in classroom, occupational/industrial courses, correspondence of equivalent value, electronic media, or other forms of self-study approved by the Registration Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Selection procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any measure, combination of measures, or procedure used as a basis for any decision in apprenticeship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes tests (paper/pencil), performance tests, training programs, probationary periods, physical/educational/work experience requirements, informal interviews, unscored applications, and the full range of assessment techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Work process schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A training plan for the on-the-job component that outlines a sequence of measurable competency benchmarks for job-related skills whose cumulative acquisition leads to occupational proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Supportive services
rubrics_metrics.description: Services such as transportation, childcare, dependent care, housing, and needs-related payments necessary to enable participation and success in registered apprenticeship and CTE apprenticeship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: A shift of apprenticeship registration from one program to another or from one employer within a program to another employer within the same program, where apprentice and affected sponsors/committee agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Underserved communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons from historically marginalized communities or populations adversely affected by persistent discrimination, inequality, or poverty, including women; persons of color (Black, Latino, Indigenous, Native American, Asian American, Native Hawaiian, Pacific Islander); individuals with disabilities; persons adhering to particular religious beliefs; veterans and military spouses; LGBTQ+ persons; and individuals with barriers to employment as defined in WIOA sec. 3(24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Undue hardship (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to provision of an accommodation, 'undue hardship' means significant difficulty or expense incurred by a sponsor when considered in light of specified factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors to consider include nature and net cost of accommodation (consider tax credits/deductions/outside funding); overall financial resources of facility/facilities and number of persons employed; overall resources and size of sponsor and program; type of operations including workforce composition and geographic separateness; and impact of accommodation on facility operations and other apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupations suitable for registered apprenticeship — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the Administrator can determine whether an occupation is suitable for registered apprenticeship; those determined suitable are eligible for local registration for Federal purposes by a Registration Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupations suitability minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To be deemed suitable, an occupation must: (1) be commonly recognized as a standalone, distinct occupation throughout an industry/sector; (2) lead to a sustainable career; (3) be trainable via a structured on-the-job apprenticeship enabling acquisition of necessary knowledge, skills, techniques, and competencies; (4) require completion of at least 2,000 hours of on-the-job training and at least an average of 144 hours of off-the-job related instruction per 2,000 hours of OJT to obtain proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The minimum number of hours must involve at least 2,000 hours of on-the-job training; related instruction cannot be less than the minimum average of 144 hours per 2,000 OJT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required for new occupation suitability determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants seeking a new determination must submit documentation sufficient to show each suitability requirement is met and additional supporting materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items: (1) documentation showing compliance with requirements (b)(1)-(4); (2) a work process schedule and explanation of how its skills will lead to proficiency via structured OJT; (3) documentation of industry standard minimum OJT hours (must be at least 2,000); (4) related instruction outline and explanation based on industry standards describing curriculum and hours (not less than average 144 hours per 2,000 OJT); (5) documentation of any interim credentials, recognized postsecondary credentials, or occupational licenses related to the occupation and whether optional or required during apprenticeship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment and decision timeline for occupation suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator will solicit public comment on suitability submissions for at least 30 days and make a determination within 90 days after a complete application is received, subject to extension or requests for more information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator may extend the 90-day period with notice and may request additional data; will maintain an up-to-date public list of suitability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for denying occupation suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: An occupation will not be approved where: (1) application is incomplete; (2) any of the minimum requirements are not met; (3) proposed scope is confined to a narrowly specialized subset of skills not readily transferable between employers; (4) occupation duplicates significant work processes of another approved occupation but does not lead to a more advanced occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If denied, the Administrator will provide a written explanation to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review of suitability determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator will periodically review continued suitability, relevance, and applicability of a work process schedule and related instruction outline for an approved occupation at least every 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on review, Administrator may determine occupation remains suitable or requires adjustments; if revisions are made, existing programs must update their work process schedules or related instruction outlines to align with changes before next training cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — requirement for written standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Each registered apprenticeship program must have a written set of standards of apprenticeship governing conduct and operation, and such standards must include specified provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — eligibility requirements and minimum starting age
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include minimum eligibility requirements for entry, including minimum starting age not less than 16 years except where higher age required by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — sponsor selection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include the sponsor's procedures for selection of apprentices, which must comply with part 30 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — recruitment area
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include the sponsor's relevant recruitment area for selection of apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — term of apprenticeship and minimums
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must set the term of the apprenticeship sufficient for attaining proficiency and must include: (i) a term of paid OJT reflecting customary industry standard, not less than 2,000 hours; (ii) related instruction hours reflecting customary industry standard but not less than an average of 144 hours for every 2,000 hours of OJT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term must be sufficient for apprentice to attain knowledge, skills, techniques, competencies relevant to covered occupations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — covered occupations, work processes, and related instruction outlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must identify the program's covered occupation(s), work process schedule(s), and related instruction outline(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — related instruction providers and instructional methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must identify related instruction provider(s) and methods used to deliver related instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — trainer/instructor qualifications documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include documentation that trainers' and instructors' qualifications and experience satisfy the requirements in §29.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — interim credentials and post-completion credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe any interim credential issued during the apprenticeship, any industry-portable qualification/license/certification an apprentice will receive or be eligible for upon completion, and any postsecondary credit available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — counting related instruction as hours worked
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must state whether time spent in related instruction will be counted as hours worked, and if so, the wage rate and fringe benefits for those hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — assessment and feedback process
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe the process for regularly assessing and providing feedback on apprentice acquisition of job-related knowledge, skills, and competencies during OJT, and may grant advanced standing for accelerated attainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — end-point assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must specify the end-point assessment process for certifying successful attainment of all necessary knowledge, skills, and competencies at program conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — probationary period limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include a probationary period that is reasonable relative to full term, credited toward completion, not to exceed 25% of total program length or 1 year, whichever is shorter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — compliance with law
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must state that the program will be conducted in accordance with all applicable Federal, State, or local laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — worker rights and protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must acknowledge apprentices are entitled to same worker allowances, rights, and protections as similarly situated non-apprentice employees under applicable laws (e.g., family and medical leave, workers' compensation, health and retirement benefits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — facilities and equipment attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include an attestation by the sponsor, supported by documentation, that the program will provide adequate, safe, and accessible facilities and equipment compliant with disability, occupational safety, and health laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — safety training attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include an attestation by the sponsor that the program will provide adequate, industry-recognized safety training in both OJT and related instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — wages and fringe benefits requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must state wages and fringe benefits and meet requirements: (i) entry wage not less than FLSA minimum where applicable unless higher law/contract applies; (ii) graduated schedule of increasing wages from entry to journeyworker that reflects progressive, measurable acquisition of skills (unless different schedule required by law or collective bargaining); (iii) final wage must be at least 75% of journeyworker wage paid by employer for that occupation (subject to law or collective bargaining exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduated schedule must include at least one incremental wage step during first 2,000 hours and additional increments at reasonable intervals for longer programs, except where collective bargaining requires otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — disclosure of unreimbursed costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must state approximate amount of any unreimbursed costs, expenses, or fees apprentices may incur; such costs must be necessary, reasonable, not impose substantial or inequitable financial barriers, and comply with applicable wage laws and acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs must comply with FLSA, Davis-Bacon, McNamara-O'Hara Service Contract Act, and implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — apprentice-to-journeyworker ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must specify a numeric ratio of apprentices to journeyworkers consistent with safety, health, supervision, and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratio must be consistent with collective bargaining agreements and applicable laws; must be specific and clearly described as to application to particular workforce/workplace/job site/department/plant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — advanced standing and credit process
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe the process to reduce usual term of OJT or related instruction due to prior learning, training, acquired experience, or accelerated progress; process must be fair, transparent, equitable, objectively identify/assess/document prior learning and result in advanced standing/credit and increased wage commensurate with progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — provisions for transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, standards must provide for transfer of apprentices between registered programs involving the same occupation with agreement of apprentice and affected sponsors/committees, and must require documentation and a new apprenticeship agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer requirements: documentation of accrued related instruction and OJT from originating sponsor; transfer to the same occupation; execution of a new apprenticeship agreement after the transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — recordkeeping requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must require the program sponsor and participating employers to create and maintain all apprenticeship records detailed at §29.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — Equal Opportunity Pledge and EEO compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include sponsor's Equal Opportunity Pledge pursuant to §30.3(c) and an attestation that program will be operated in accordance with part 30 and, where applicable, an approved State EEO plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — workplace safety and inclusion attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must attest that sponsor and participating employers will implement effective measures to promote and maintain a safe and inclusive workplace free from violence, harassment, intimidation, and retaliation against apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — Support for Veterans assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs registered on or after Sept 22, 2020, standards must include attestation that sponsor will provide written assurances required under section 2(b)(1) of the Support for Veterans in Effective Apprenticeships Act of 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Pub. L. 116-134 and 29 U.S.C. 50c.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of apprenticeship — complaint contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include contact information (name, address, telephone, email) for the individual with authority to receive, process, and make disposition of complaints under the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group program sponsor responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registered apprenticeship program provides training to apprentices employed by participating employers in a group program (e.g., under a collective bargaining agreement or program standards adoption), the sponsor is responsible for specified duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsor must (1) obtain attestation that participating employer agrees to abide by part requirements before admission; (2) obtain written disclosure of any final agency determinations that the participating employer has violated applicable laws (OSHA, wage/hour, financial mismanagement, EEO, harassment/assault protections, etc.), including description and remedial actions, before admission; (3) actively monitor each participating employer after admission to assess adherence to minimum standards and regulatory requirements in this part and part 30.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — requirement to be written and signed
rubrics_metrics.description: All apprenticeship programs registered by a Registration Agency must develop a written apprenticeship agreement containing terms and conditions of employment and training, signed prior to start by apprentice, parent/guardian if under 18, program sponsor, and any participating employers who adopted sponsor's standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — provision of documents prior to signing
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to signing, apprentice must be furnished with a copy of the proposed apprenticeship agreement and program standards and be given reasonable opportunity to inspect and review them; after signing, the sponsor must deliver a copy of the executed agreement and standards to the apprentice no later than the apprenticeship start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — required identifying/contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must contain apprentice identifying/contact information including date of birth and, voluntarily, Social Security number; contact information for Registration Agency, program sponsor, and participating employer(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — identification of occupation and inclusion of schedules/outlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must identify the occupation in which the apprentice is to be trained and include copies of the associated work process schedule and related instruction outline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — incorporation of program standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must incorporate the program's standards of apprenticeship either directly or by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — roles, duties, and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must describe respective roles, duties, and responsibilities of apprentice, sponsor, and participating employer, including providing information to apprentices about rights and protections and how to file complaints with Registration Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — term dates and probationary period
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must state the beginning date and expected duration of the apprenticeship, beginning date of OJT, and duration of the probationary period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — wages and fringe benefits details
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must include a detailed statement of entry wage, graduated wage scale over the term, the journeyworker wage, and any fringe benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — disclosure of expected minimum hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must disclose expected minimum number of hours allocated to OJT and to related instruction during the apprenticeship term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — methods to measure progress and end-point assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must describe methods used to measure competency progress and the program's end-point assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — supportive services description
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must describe any supportive services available to the apprentice (childcare, transportation, equipment, tools, or other services provided by sponsor or partners to address barriers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — disclosure of unreimbursed costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must state nature and amount of any unreimbursed costs, expenses, or fees the apprentice may incur during participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — post-completion credits/credentials/qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must describe recognized postsecondary credits, credentials, and occupational qualifications the apprentice will receive or be eligible for upon successful completion and any additional conditions to satisfy qualification/licensure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — compliance with part 30 and EEO
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must include a statement by parties that they will adhere to applicable requirements of part 30 of this title and, where applicable, an approved State EEO plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — related instruction pay and scheduling statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must state whether the apprentice is paid wages and fringe benefits during related instruction, the wage rate if paid, and whether related instruction is provided during work hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — dispute contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must provide contact information of authority designated under the program to receive/process/decide controversies or disputes arising when they cannot be resolved locally or per collective bargaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — advanced standing/credit procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreement must describe processes and procedures for granting advanced standing or credit consistent with §29.8(a)(20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — prohibition on non-compete provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors or participating employers cannot include or impose non-compete provisions restricting apprentice's ability to compete with sponsor/participating employer or to seek employment with another employer prior to program completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — restrictions on non-disclosure provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors/participating employers cannot include non-disclosure provisions that prevent the worker from working in the same field after employment or that restrict an apprentice's ability to file complaints with Registration Agency or government bodies; subject to these restrictions, confidentiality provisions protecting trade secrets or confidential business information are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — submission to Registration Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsor must submit a completed copy of the executed apprenticeship agreement for each registered apprentice to the program's Registration Agency within 30 days of execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — cancellation during probation
rubrics_metrics.description: The apprenticeship agreement may be cancelled by either party without cause during the probationary period specified in the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship agreement — cancellation or suspension after probation
rubrics_metrics.description: After the probationary period, the apprentice may cancel at any time; the sponsor may suspend or cancel only for good cause and must provide written notice to the apprentice explaining cause and written notice to Registration Agency of the cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration — required application materials (work process & instruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for registration, prospective sponsor must submit electronically a work process schedule and related instruction outline consistent with an occupation deemed suitable by the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration — required application materials (standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration application must include the standards of apprenticeship for the proposed program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration — required application materials (apprenticeship agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration application must include the apprenticeship agreement for the apprenticeship program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration — equitable recruitment and retention plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include a written plan for equitable recruitment and retention of apprentices, including those from underserved communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan should address outreach and strategies to recruit and retain underrepresented groups and comply with EEO requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration — demonstration of financial capacity/resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include information showing that prospective sponsor possesses and can maintain the financial capacity and other resources necessary to operate the proposed program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration — disclosure of prior agency determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include disclosure in writing of all instances where a Federal, State, or local agency issued a final determination that the prospective sponsor (or officers/employees) violated applicable laws pertaining to occupational safety/health, labor standards (wage/hour), financial mismanagement/abuse, EEO, protections against harassment/assault, or other workplace laws; must include description and remedial actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure is required prior to registration to inform Registration Agency consideration of sponsor suitability.
